scope: Read-only pixel review of the eleven live Fairy growth, target, leaf, helpful-cue and danger-cue PNGs named by scripts/games/fairy.gd. Scores cover only source identity, finish, edges and within-family consistency. Animation, contact, current composition, Mobile mounting, device readability, child response and owner acceptance are null.

method.pixel_inspection: Each 1024x1024 PNG was opened at original detail with view_image.
method.hashing: SHA-256 over exact repository file bytes.
method.runtime_trace: Literal bindings and configured visual_size values were read from scripts/games/fairy.gd.
prior_evidence_reused: audit/minigame_art_quality_2026-09-05/current_coverage_gap_followup.json establishes the bounded registry additions and source bindings; it assigns no quality scores.

audit/MASTER_AUDIT_2026-08-09.md records Fairy as 3/5 because the runtime remains a spatial scroller and state-local composition evidence is incomplete; it explicitly warns against recoloring approved art from source-average metrics alone.
method.limits: Source inspection cannot establish the appearance of Sprite3D alpha-cut mounting, depth, cue overlays, rotation, scale, figure-ground contrast, motion, hit response or bloom timing. The current Sprite3D route is measured 3D migration debt and no source score accepts that runtime medium.

bug_targets.binding: FS_BUG_ART cycles jewel, moth and firefly across recurring targets; the same sources are also reused for hazards at 7.2, 7.4 and 10.5.

boss_leaf.binding: FS_BOSS_LEAF_ART forms the destructible outer ring.

helpful_cue.binding: FS_HELPFUL_CUE_ART is used for six gates, the reticle, and overlays on boss leaves.

danger_cue.binding: FS_DANGER_CUE_ART surrounds bug/hazard sources and is also the projectile/orb source.

assets.evidence: The cracked plum seed shell, dark opening and tiny mint-purple sprout make the starting state unmistakable. Layered cracks and navy silhouette are controlled; the sprout already establishes the later family's curl and palette.
Four broad mint leaves, purple tips, central bud and the retained curled stem clearly advance the seed. Broad value bands and uninterrupted outline support reduction.
The enlarged purple bud becomes the dominant focus while leaf placement, vein language, curled stem and mint-lavender palette continue directly from sprout.
Separated inner petals and the first visible clustered center provide a clear intermediate opening state without changing the plant's silhouette family or materials.
Multiple concentric petal rows, bright clustered center and retained leaf/stem structure produce a strong, authored payoff with clear continuity from opening.
Oval beetle shell, segmented legs and antennae are distinct. Coral floral shell marks, navy-purple body and cyan highlights fit the Fairy target palette while retaining a broad silhouette.
Large bilateral wings and furry segmented body read immediately as a moth. Moon, star and teardrop motifs are polished and use the same navy, lavender and mint family.
The pink glowing abdomen, paired lavender wing covers and compact beetle body distinguish the firefly from both other targets. Highlight and outline treatment stays within the same polished family.
One large mint leaf with purple tip, strong central vein and navy edge directly repeats the boss foliage language. Its simple silhouette is appropriate for six-copy reuse.

Six rounded mint petals form an unmistakably open passage; gold rounded stamens reinforce a friendly reward cue. The watercolor grain is more tactile than the smoother bug cards but remains inside the storybook material range.

Alternating long plum thorns and coral points create a strong avoid silhouette that is categorically different from the rounded helpful gate. Navy outline and watercolor grain link it to the paired cue.

family_findings.growth_continuity: Strong at source: curled stem, four-leaf base, purple tips, navy contours and central bud/flower enlarge in an ordered visual progression.
family_findings.target_discrimination: Strong at source: beetle oval, moth wings and firefly glow have distinct dominant silhouettes while sharing palette and outline language.
family_findings.cue_pair: Strong at source: rounded mint/gold open ring versus pointed coral/plum thorn ring provides a clear semantic contrast.
family_findings.decision: Retain all eleven existing sources. No visually evidenced source dimension in this bounded review is below 4.5, so source replacement or regeneration is not justified.

unassessed_runtime_risks: The five growth sources are separate cards; still pixels do not prove transition timing, scale continuity, contact response or bloom settle.
Cue overlays may cover bug or leaf identity at their configured relative scales; source inspection cannot score that composition.
The helpful cue is reused as gate, reticle and leaf overlay, and the danger cue as halo and projectile; role readability must be checked in each mounted state.
Bug sources are repurposed as jelly, urchin and eel hazards; source identity scores do not prove those renamed runtime roles read truthfully.
All reviewed cards currently mount through Sprite3D in a spatial scroller, which remains game-wide 2D migration debt regardless of source quality.
Actual phone-scale alpha-cut edges, figure-ground contrast, density, touch/contact feedback and child understanding remain unreviewed.
required_next_evidence: Current Mobile captures of each boss state at its configured scale, including every transition and bloom settle.
Representative live frames pairing each bug with its danger halo and each boss leaf with its helpful overlay.
Separate mounted review of helpful gate, reticle, danger halo and orb roles.
Canvas-port evidence and phone/device review before any game-wide acceptance claim.
